findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the disposer
findings.body: After cleanup is invoked, the socket remains subscribed and later messages still invoke the stale handler. Repeated attach/cleanup cycles retain handlers and cause duplicate processing. Restore the call to `socket.off("message", handler)`.

findings.title: [P2] Clear the polling interval in the disposer
findings.body: Calling cleanup no longer stops polling, so `refresh` continues after teardown. Repeated start/stop cycles accumulate background work, and the live interval can prevent a Node.js process from exiting. Retain and clear the timer as before.

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the disposer
findings.body:

findings.title: [P2] Cancel the interval when polling is stopped
findings.body:
Calling the returned stop function no longer stops polling, so `refresh` continues every second after teardown. In Node.js, the retained interval can also prevent graceful process exit; repeated start/stop cycles accumulate concurrent pollers.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore socket listener removal to prevent resource-exhaustion attacks
findings.body:
The returned disposer no longer unregisters the handler. In a long-lived process where an attacker can repeatedly trigger subscription setup/teardown, handlers and their captured state accumulate indefinitely; each message then invokes every stale handler, enabling memory and CPU exhaustion.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Clear polling intervals when callers dispose them
findings.body:
Every invocation now creates a permanent interval. If an attacker can repeatedly trigger a lifecycle that starts and disposes polling, timers and refresh closures accumulate without bound and execute every second, causing sustained CPU, memory, and potentially outbound-request exhaustion.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore removal of the message listener in the disposer
findings.body:
When callers invoke the returned cleanup while the socket remains alive, the handler and its captured state stay retained and continue processing every message. Repeated attach/cleanup cycles accumulate listeners, memory use, and per-message work.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Retain and clear the polling interval in the disposer
findings.body:
After callers invoke the returned cleanup, the interval still runs every second and retains `refresh` and its captured state. In Node.js it also keeps the event loop alive, so disposed polling can cause unbounded background work and prevent process termination.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
